raw_response:
*Sitting down, thinking about the year ahead...*

Aiya, 3.5 mu isn't much land, but it's what we have. My husband and eldest son both go into town for work most of the year, so the fields are mostly my job, same as always. My daughter-in-law helps when she can, but she's got the little ones to watch. With six mouths to feed, I can't afford to mess this up.

**The wheat I already planted back in October.** Same as every year — one bag of compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15 kind, one bag per mu) worked into the soil before I put the seed in. I bought fresh seed this time from the shop at the crossroads, the same variety my neighbor Old Wang uses because his fields looked good last June. Maybe 30 kuai a mu for seed. The wheat came up alright before winter.

Now that spring is coming, I need to think about topdressing and water. When the wheat greens up and starts standing up (what the young people call 拔节, jointing), I'll put down urea — maybe half a bag per mu, about 20-25 jin. I watch the leaves. If they look yellowish I put a little more, if they look dark green I hold back. My grandmother taught me that.

For water, the well is there but every time I irrigate it costs money for the electricity and the pipe. I'll water three times if the sky doesn't help me — once before the really cold days if the soil is dry, once at jointing with the urea, and once when the grain is filling out in May. If it rains good, I skip one. Last year I only watered twice because spring rain came and I saved maybe 100 kuai.

Weeds I spray once with the cheap herbicide everyone uses. If I see the aphids on the heads later I'll spray once more but usually it's fine.

Wheat should give me 400 jin per mu, maybe 450 if the weather is kind. That's what I usually get.

**Then right after wheat harvest in early June, it's maize.** This is the tight part — the combine cuts the wheat one day, and within three or four days I need the maize in the ground or it won't finish before the cold. I hire the no-till planter from the village (around 30 kuai per mu) because there's no time to plow properly between the two crops anyway. 

For maize I buy hybrid seed every year — you can't save it, everyone knows that. Probably 60 kuai a mu for the seed. I put one bag of compound fertilizer down when it's planted. If the maize looks weak when it's knee-high I'll throw some urea between the rows, but on this land with the wheat straw left behind, usually one bag is enough. I don't like wasting fertilizer when money is tight.

Maize I usually don't irrigate unless summer is really dry. July and August usually give enough rain. Maybe once at tasseling time if I have to. I spray once for the corn borer in July, that's all.

Maize should give 450 jin per mu, similar to the neighbors.

**My worries this year:** Fertilizer prices went up again last year, I heard. If one bag is over 150 kuai now I might stretch a bag across a bit more than one mu — I've done that before in hard years. The yield drops a little but the money saved helps. I also need to keep some cash for when the grandchildren need school things.
